Master’s degree in business, public administration, health administration, or a related field.
Five (5) or more years of progressively responsible experience in business operations, administration, financial management, program coordination, or project management.
Experience working in complex research, academic, healthcare, or highly regulated environment.
Three (3) to Five (5) years of experience coordinating work across multiple functional areas and stakeholders without direct supervisory authority.
Experience supporting compliance, safety, audit, records management, or business continuity activities in a regulated environment.

Reporting to the Division of Laboratory Animal Medicine (DLAM) Executive Director, the Department Administrative Manager serves as a senior individual contributor responsible for coordinating and administering core departmental business operations. The position provides operational, financial, analytical, project management, and administrative support across a complex research and service environment. Working in close partnership with departmental leadership and centralized DGSOM and UCLA administrative offices, the Manager monitors budgets and business processes, coordinates human resources and procurement activities, supports facilities and compliance needs, develops reports and recommendations, and advances department priorities. This role will focus on execution, coordination, analysis, and advisory support.
Demonstrated discretion and sound judgment when handling confidential, sensitive, or high-impact information.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, and collaborative tracking tools.
Thorough knowledge of administrative operations, including financial administration, procurement, human resources coordination, facilities, records, and project management.
Knowledge of University administrative systems, policies, and procedures related to finance, procurement, human resources, and research administration.
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex operational and financial information, identify risks and alternatives, and develop clear, practical recommendations.
Knowledge of budgeting, financial analysis, reconciliation, forecasting, internal controls, and management reporting.
Ability to interpret and apply policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements in a complex institutional environment.
Strong project management skills, including planning, prioritization, risk tracking, stakeholder coordination, and timely delivery of results.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including preparation of concise reports, presentations, procedures, and executive-level correspondence.
Ability to establish cooperative working relationships and influence outcomes across organizational levels without relying on direct authority.
Ability to independently organize and manage competing priorities, changing deadlines, and assignments of diverse scope.
Commitment to service, continuous improvement, collaboration, accountability, and inclusive workplace practices.
